name: Solgrip Tamarind-Chili Pulls
manufacturer: Solgrip Foods (Corponation subsidiary of Veltane Consumer)
description: Stretchy, high-density synth-chews coated in a tamarind-chili dust that blooms from sour to slow heat. A staple in Tier 1 and 2 vending rows, sold in strips of six wrapped in foil.
flavor_profile: Bright tamarind pucker up front, then a slow-building chili warmth that lingers on the back of the throat; slightly waxy chew texture
cultural_context: Solgrip Pulls are so ubiquitous on the Shelf that 'got a pull?' functions as casual small-talk and an offer of goodwill. Sharing a strip is a minor social ritual. Street kids use the foil wrappers for origami currency markers.
story_hooks: A Tier 1 fixer uses Solgrip wrappers as dead-drop markers — a specific fold left on a vent grate signals a meet.

A Veltane quality auditor discovers that the Shelf-district batches contain an unlicensed mild analgesic compound — someone in the supply chain is doing something unauthorized, possibly compassionate, possibly profitable.
A child hands a runner a strip of Solgrip as payment for a favor; the runner later realizes it was the last food the kid had.
